chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: Indeed, the believer holds a most excellent station with Allah, Mighty and Majestic—three times. He surely tries him with affliction, then takes out his soul, limb by limb, from his body, while he praises Allah for that.

key_terms.اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, before whom the believer holds rank
key_terms.الْبَلَاءِ: affliction or trial by which the believer is tested
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the faithful believer whose spiritual station is being described
key_terms.جَسَدِهِ: his body, from which the soul is withdrawn
key_terms.عُضْوًا عُضْوًا: limb by limb, expressing the severity and gradual nature of suffering
key_terms.لَبِأَفْضَلِ مَكَانٍ: in a most excellent station or position
key_terms.نَفْسَهُ: his soul, taken by Allah at death
key_terms.يَحْمَدُ اللَّهَ: he praises Allah, showing gratitude and steadfast faith

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the rank of the believer during affliction and death?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the muʾmin has a lofty rank before Allah عزّ وجلّ, and that severe afflictions do not indicate divine abandonment. Rather, even in intense suffering and at death, the true believer remains in praise of Allah, showing sabr and spiritual nearness.
